Analysis.description: Analysis judges the new version by metrics during the soak: after the traffic switch each metric's query is asked of a Prometheus, and a value outside its bounds, a number of evaluations in a row, sends traffic back to the previous version.

address.description: Address is the base URL of the Prometheus (or of anything that answers its query API: Mimir, VictoriaMetrics, Thanos), such as http://127.0.0.1:9090. A path prefix is kept (https://metrics.example.com/prometheus). It holds no credentials: put an authenticating proxy in front, on this server. Default http://127.0.0.1:9090.

metrics.description: Metrics are the gates, at most 5. Every one must hold.

App.description: App is one container the agent deploys and keeps running.

analysis.description: Analysis judges the new version by Prometheus queries during the soak and rolls back when they leave their bounds. See Analysis.

build.description: Build, when set, lets the dashboard have this agent build the image from a source archive (a GitHub App installation) instead of pulling one CI built. See Build.

database.description: Database is the database the agent creates for the app on its managed PostgreSQL. See AppDatabase.

deploy.description: Deploy chooses how the app is deployed. See Deploy.

domains.description: Domains route public hostnames to the app through the reverse proxy. An app with domains is deployed blue/green: the new container runs next to the old one and traffic switches once it is healthy, so there is no outage. It needs Port and the top-level proxy section.

drain.description: Drain is how long the previous version keeps running after the proxy has switched to the new one, so that requests a proxy worker still routes to it are not refused. Default 5s; 0s stops it at once.

environment.description: Stage is the environment (the field is named so because App already has an Environment method).

health_path.description: HealthPath, if set, is requested over HTTP on the new container's port and must answer 2xx before traffic switches. It checks the port the new container really listens on, which an image HEALTHCHECK with a fixed port would not.

health_timeout.description: HealthTimeout bounds the wait for the new container to become healthy. Default 90s.

image.description: Image is the repository without tag or digest. Deploy requests only choose the tag or digest, never the repository: whoever can call the deploy API cannot make the agent run an arbitrary image.

keep_images.description: KeepImages is how many of the most recently deployed versions stay on the server (the running one included); older images of this app are removed after a successful deployment. Default 3.

log.description: Log sets how Docker keeps the container's output. Without it, logs are rotated (json-file, 10 MiB, 3 files): an app that logs a lot must not fill the disk.

network.description: Network is a network name, or "host".

port.description: Port is the port of a blue/green app: the container port the proxy forwards to (the agent publishes it on a random loopback host port), or, with network: host, the two host ports the app alternates between and the variable that tells it which one to listen on. See PortSpec.

previews.description: Previews is the template of the app's per-pull-request environments. See Previews.

project.description: Project and Environment place the app in the dashboard's Projects view: the same project on several servers (or several apps of one server) with a different environment each, such as production and staging. They label only: nothing here changes how the app runs. Both are optional; the dashboard reads a missing project as the app's name and a missing environment as "production".

publish.description: Publish are the fixed port mappings "[hostip:]hostport:containerport[/proto]".

release.description: Release runs between the pull and the switch: backup, migration.

restart.description: Restart is the Docker restart policy: no, always, unless-stopped or on-failure. Default unless-stopped.

soak.description: Soak is how long the previous version keeps running after the traffic switch (and the drain) while the new one is watched; if it fails the traffic goes back to the previous version. Default 30s; 0s turns it off. Only for blue/green apps.

source.description: Source links the app to the repository it is built from. See Source.

stable_after.description: StableAfter is how long a container must keep running (an image without HEALTHCHECK) or keep reporting healthy (an image with one, only when the file sets stable_after) before the traffic switches. Default 10s.

stop_timeout.description: StopTimeout is the grace period before the old container is killed. Default 10s; 0s kills at once.

verify.description: Verify lists pages requested on the new container during the soak, next to health_path.

AppDatabase.description: AppDatabase is the database the agent creates on its own PostgreSQL instance for an app: a database and a role of the app's name, the URL stored in the variable EnvKey of the app, the password in PasswordFile.

env_key.description: EnvKey is the variable that holds its URL; default DATABASE_URL.

name.description: Name is the name of the database and of its role; default: the name of the app.

password_file.description: PasswordFile is the file the agent keeps the role's password in. Absolute path.

BackupDestination.description: BackupDestination is exactly one of a local directory or an S3-compatible bucket.

Backups.description: Backups says when a database is backed up, how long backups are kept and where they go.

destinations.description: Destinations are the places backups go; every one must succeed.

keep.description: Keep is how many of the newest backups are kept; default 14.

keep_days.description: KeepDays also deletes the backups older than that many days; 0 = off. The newest backup is never deleted.

keep_pre_deploy.description: KeepPreDeploy is how many backups taken before a deployment (a `backup` release step) are kept, apart from keep: the same count applies to the safety backups taken before an overwrite restore. Default 5.

recipients.description: Recipients are age X25519 public keys: the backup can only be read with one of the matching secret keys, which the agent never holds.

Build.description: Build lets the agent build the app's image itself from a source archive the dashboard hands it (a GitHub App installation: see docs/hosting.md), instead of pulling an image CI built. The agent downloads the source, builds it with Docker on this server, tags the result "<image>:<commit sha>" locally and deploys it through the usual pipeline. Nothing is pushed to a registry, and nothing builds unless a build is requested: declaring this block only makes the app able to. A build executes the repository's Dockerfile on this server (or the Dockerfile of its preset). Build inputs are separate from deploy inputs: the arguments are not secret, and no secret (the app's env, its registries) is ever given to a build.

args.description: Args are build arguments. They are NOT secret: they appear in the image history and in this document.

context.description: Context is the subdirectory of the repository sent to Docker as the build context. Default ".".

cpus.description: CPUs caps their CPU time, in cores. Default 2.

database.description: Database lets the build use the app's managed database: its URL is passed to the build as a build argument (the one case where a managed database's password reaches a build), and the build runs on the network that reaches it. For a build that queries its database to build (static pages filled from it) on a database that is new and empty.

dockerfile.description: Dockerfile is the path of the Dockerfile inside Context. Default "Dockerfile". Not with a preset.

install.description: Install, BuildCommand, Start, OutputDir, Node, SPA and Standalone tune a preset; they are refused without one. Their defaults are in presets.go.

max_source.description: MaxSource is the largest source archive that is accepted, such as "512m". Default 512m.

memory.description: Memory caps the memory of the build's containers, such as "2g". Default 2g.

network.description: Network is the network the build's containers run on: empty is the engine's default bridge, "host" is the server's own network, any other value the name of a user-defined Docker network (such as the one the managed PostgreSQL lives on). Host is for a build that must reach something only the server sees (a database on 127.0.0.1 that a framework queries while it builds): the build's code then sees every port the server listens on, so turn it on only for a repository you trust to that level. A named network gives the build the containers on it, no more. Empty with `database: true` picks the network that reaches the app's managed database.

only.description: Only makes the app a builder: this server builds its image and keeps it, nothing runs here. The dashboard then sends the image to the app that runs it, on another server (a build needs memory a small server of a site does not have to spare, and a server that builds can build for several). A build-only app has no container, no routing, no release steps and no volumes, and cannot be deployed or rolled back: its image is only built and exported. Deprecated: a server that builds for others declares build_limits, and the builds come through POST /v1/builds (see legacy_builder.go). Still read, with a deprecation warning, until the legacy code is removed.

platform.description: Platform is the platform the image is built for, "linux/amd64" or "linux/arm64". Empty builds for the engine's own. It is what lets a build machine of another architecture (an Apple-silicon Mac) produce what the server runs.

preset.description: Preset makes the agent write the Dockerfile itself: nextjs, node, vite or static (see presets.go). Empty builds the repository's own Dockerfile. A preset and a dockerfile are alternatives.

source_hosts.description: SourceHosts are the hosts the source may be downloaded from (an exact match on the host name; redirects may only go to these too, and to GitHub's codeload host). For GitHub Enterprise Server, list its host.

target.description: Target is the multi-stage target to build; empty builds the last stage.

timeout.description: Timeout bounds the whole build, source download included. Default 15m, at most 1h.

ContainerAction.description: ContainerAction runs Command in a throwaway container with the environment, volumes and network of an app.

app.description: App is the app a job runs in, from the version it is serving. A release step never sets it: it runs in the app being deployed.

image.description: Image overrides the repository of a release step's container, for a tool that is not in the runtime image (a migrator). It is deployed with the same tag as the app, so CI builds both. A job never sets it.

Database.description: Database is an existing PostgreSQL server the agent can see, back up and restore. Nothing here is a secret: the password and the S3 secret key stay in files. The databases the agent creates itself are not written here: they are the database of an app (App.Database), and Config.Databases lists them too once the file is parsed.

managed.description: Managed marks a database the agent created on its own PostgreSQL instance (see POST /v1/postgres/databases): a database and a role named like the entry, the instance's host and network, the password in PasswordFile. They are declared by App.Database; App is the app the database was created for and EnvKey the variable holding its URL. The three keys are also read from the legacy `managed: true` entry of a file that could not be migrated (see legacy.go).

network.description: Network is the Docker network of the throwaway containers that reach the server; default host.

password_file.description: PasswordFile holds the password; it is read at every run, so a rotation needs no restart.

project.description: Project groups the database with the others of a project in the dashboard (see Job.Project). Optional.

ssl_mode.description: SSLMode is PGSSLMODE: disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca or verify-full.

version.description: Version is the PostgreSQL major version of the client tools; empty means the server's.

Deploy.description: Deploy is how the app is deployed. Without it the strategy follows the routing: an app with domains or a port is switched, any other is replaced.

strategy.description: Strategy is "switch" (blue/green; needs a port or domains) or "replace" (in place; no domains, no port).

Job.description: Job is something the agent runs on a schedule: an HTTP call to an app (the cron endpoints GitHub Actions used to hit), a command on the host (a backup script, a log purge), or a command in a one-off container of an app. Its Schedule says when and how long, its Action what: exactly one of http, host and container.

project.description:
Project groups the job with the others of a project in the dashboard: the same label as App.Project. It is optional (the dashboard then derives it from the app the job calls). A job in projects.d/

.yaml is of the project

: unset is filled in, another value is an error. A backup job takes its database's.

JobBearer.description: JobBearer names where a bearer secret comes from: File, or the variable Env of the app App (its env and env_file). Exactly one of the two.

JobHTTP.description: JobHTTP is an HTTP request. A 2xx answer is success unless ExpectStatus lists others.

bearer.description: Bearer sends "Authorization: Bearer <secret>", the secret read from a file or from an app's environment each time the job runs.

LocalDestination.description: LocalDestination is a directory on the agent's host.

Log.description: Log is how Docker keeps a container's output.

driver.description: Driver is "json-file" (the default) or "local": both rotate by size.

max_file.description: MaxFile is how many rotated files are kept. Default 3.

max_size.description: MaxSize is the size at which a log file is rotated. Default 10m.

Metric.description: Metric is one gate: a PromQL query and the bounds its value must stay within.

failure_limit.description: FailureLimit is how many evaluations in a row must be bad before the deployment is rolled back. Default 3.

interval.description: Interval is how often the query is asked. Default 10s, at least 1s. The first evaluation is one interval after the soak starts, so that a rate has samples of the new version to work on.

max.description: Max is the highest value that is fine (an error rate: 0.01). Min is the lowest (a success rate: 0.99). At least one.

name.description: Name labels the gate in the deployment's events and in the error (letters, digits, - and _).

no_data.description: NoData is what an empty answer counts as: "pass" (default; a quiet app has no traffic to judge) or "fail".

query.description: Query is a PromQL expression. {{app}}, {{container}} (the new container) and {{version}} (the image reference being deployed) are replaced by their value, escaped for a PromQL string. The query must answer a number: a scalar or an instant vector, every sample of which is judged.

Previews.description: Previews is the template of the ephemeral environments of one app (App.Previews): every pull request that CI built an image for gets an instance, named "<app>-pr-<n>", that lives until the pull request is closed, its TTL ends, or newer instances push it out. Instances are never in the apps list: they live in the agent's database. The parent app is the one that holds the template: its image repository, port and runtime settings are what an instance runs. It must be proxied with a container port (its own network), behind the Caddy driver.

domain.description: Domain is the public host pattern, with {pr} for the pull request number, in one label: pr-{pr}-shop.example.com.

env_file.description: EnvFile and Env are the instance's own environment. The parent's env_file and env are never inherited: they hold production secrets.

max.description: Max is how many instances of the app exist at once: creating one more removes the oldest. Default 5.

ttl.description: TTL is how long an instance lives after its last deployment. Default 168h.

Release.description: Release is what runs between "the new image is pulled" and "the new version takes over": typically a database backup and the schema migration. A failing step stops the deployment before anything serving was touched.

on_rollback.description: OnRollback also runs the steps when the deployment is a rollback. Off by default: re-running migrations from an older image is not what a rollback is for, and a backup before restoring old code is rarely wanted.

ReleaseStep.description: ReleaseStep is one step of the release phase: an Action (host, container or backup), with its own timeout.

continue_on_failure.description: ContinueOnFailure logs a failure as a warning and goes on, instead of aborting the deployment.

timeout.description: Timeout bounds the step; default 10 minutes.

S3Destination.description: S3Destination is a bucket reached path-style (endpoint/bucket/key).

access_key_id.description: AccessKeyID is an identifier, not a secret; the secret key is read from SecretKeyFile at every run.

Source.description: Source links an app to the repository it is built from. The agent checks the shape and never acts on it: the dashboard reads it (to deploy when a workflow succeeds, to build a pull request) and writes it. Saving it creates a configuration version and needs no redeploy.

branch.description: Branch is the git branch the app follows.

build_on.description: BuildOn lists the events that build the app: push and pull_request. Absent: nothing builds by itself.

build_server.description: BuildServer is the name of the server (as the dashboard knows it) that builds the image. Absent: the app builds where it runs.

deploy_on.description: DeployOn is "workflow" (deploy when the workflow named below succeeds) or absent (manual deploys only).

previews_workflow.description: PreviewsWorkflow names the workflow whose success on a pull request builds its preview. Absent: off.

repo.description: Repo is "owner/name". Its case is kept and matching is case-insensitive.

workflow.description: Workflow names the CI workflow whose success deploys the app. Required with deploy_on.

Verify.description: Verify is one page the soak requests on the new container, over 127.0.0.1 on the port it listens on.

path.description: Path starts with "/" and may carry a query ("/products/1?lang=fr").

status.description: Status is the status code the page must answer. 0 (the default) accepts any 2xx; a redirect is an answer, not followed, so a path that redirects needs its code (301, 302...) here.

duration.description: A length of time as a string with a unit: 90s, 5m, 1h30m, 7d. A bare number is refused, but for 0.

port.description: The container port a proxy forwards to, or a mapping: {container: 3000}, or {host: [3000, 3001], env: PORT} for an app on the host network that alternates between two host ports and is told which to listen on through the variable env.

size.description: An amount of bytes: 512m, 2g, 1GiB, or a number of bytes.
